title: unified retroactive rollout registry with safety patches
author: Maya R. Singh
description: Add a unified Rollout Registry service and API to centralize model rollout metadata, enable retroactive attachment of telemetry and automated safety patches, and provide deterministic dry-run replay for rollbacks. Motivation: teams have disparate rollout state across scheduler, serving plane, and observability — debugging regressions and issuing retroactive rollbacks is slow. This PR introduces a small, strongly-typed registry with an append-only audit ledger, an idempotent reconcile API, and a policy engine hook that can automatically apply safety patches (e.g. circuit-breaker rollback, shadow-quarantine) based on SLO breaches. Key features: 1) Rollout Registry service (new microservice) exposing REST + gRPC endpoints to register rollouts (canary/A-B/blue-green/shadow), attach telemetry pins (metrics, traces, sample requests), and mark lifecycle events (start, promote, pause, resume, rollback, finalize). 2) Retroactive binding: any telemetry ingestion pipeline can retroactively bind historical spans to a rollout by time-range and model revision, enabling post-hoc SLO checks and automatic triage. 3) Safety patch automation: declarative policies (yaml) can be registered per-customer or per-model-tag; the registry evaluates short-circuit actions and emits remediation jobs to the rollout-controller. 4) Dry-run replay harness: operators can rehearse a rollback flow against a snapshot of recent traffic in a sandbox without impacting production. 5) Console integration: lightweight UI in Redwood Console for inspecting registry entries, replay controls, and manual override. 6) Migration: new rollout_registry table and compact ledger; migration script included. Backwards compatibility: the registry is additive; existing orchestrators continue to function. Migration notes and required ops steps are in docs/rollouts/registry.md. Checklist: - [x] Design doc + Linear ENG-2741 + ENG-2819 - [x] DB migration and rollback script - [x] API + SDK client (go/python) - [x] Console UI basics - [x] Unit & integration tests - [x] Security review & KMS integration follow-up (SUP-9132) - [ ] Load testing in perf-lab (follow-up ticket created) - [x] Release notes drafted Changeset overview: commits below summarize the high-level work; files changed show main surface area. Migration: run sql/migrations/20260218_create_rollout_registry.sql then apply registry-config in Helm (templates/registry-config.yaml). Rollout policy examples included under docs/rollouts/policies/examples. Runtime hazard notes: initial rollout registry runs in a separate bounded pool; if the registry becomes slow the orchestrator falls back to local in-memory heuristics (configurable).

review_comments: Diego Marquez: Can you explain how the retro-binding handles time drift between ingestion pipelines? Suggest adding monotonic sequence ids in the ledger. Author: added monotonic sequence id to ledger and documented the delta reconciliation algorithm in docs.

Asha Patel: Security: will the registry store PII from request payloads? Please ensure redact-by-default and KMS envelope keys. Author: registry only stores request metadata (hashes and sampling pointers); added KMS integration and redact tests; SUP-9132 filed for compliance audit.
Jonah Brooks: Tests look good but add an e2e scenario with a shadow-quarantine policy applied automatically. Author: added an e2e test that simulates SLO breach and asserts remediation job emission.
Diego Marquez: Suggest exposing a lightweight metrics endpoint for registry health and queue depth. Author: added prometheus metrics and a Console health indicator.
release_notes: Introduce Rollout Registry: centralizes rollout lifecycle metadata, enables retroactive telemetry binding and automated safety patches. Docs and migration scripts included. Operators must run the DB migration and add registry-config to Helm; see docs/rollouts/registry.md.
